$comment: The reassurance line, as a table of inputs and the two strings both phones must produce.
ONE FILE, THREE READERS: test/reassurance.test.js checks it is exhaustive,
ReassuranceParityTest.kt runs the Kotlin against it, and ReassuranceParityTests.swift
runs the Swift. Change the rule and this file has to change, which fails both apps
until both are updated — which is the whole point, because the rule is written twice.
WHY A FIXTURE AND NOT A GREP. test/reassurance.test.js asserted parity by matching
the word `quietFor` in both sources. That passes whether Kotlin's floor is 90 seconds
and Swift's is 120: both files contain the word, the phones disagree, nothing is red.
A table of inputs and expected outputs is the only kind of parity a text search
